valley.drawingAlt: A ring of toadstools under one rain cloud. Four stakes in the grass mark where the rain can fall.
locals: The cloud rains where the most of us point. That is the rule, and a rule is a rule.
Mossbank and Rootstep split our votes again, and the rain went somewhere neither of them wanted.
Ambry counts every chit twice, and then once more for luck.

notes.title: The split vote
notes.science: When two close choices share their fans, a third choice can win with fewer votes than either.
notes.limits: Real elections have many more voters, and many more reasons to vote.
notes.counter: Plurality is easy to count and easy to trust, and that has value.
notes.question: Which rule would you trust with the rain?

sources.label: To Build a Better Ballot, Nicky Case
Voting Methods, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

notes.title: Other ways to count
notes.science: Approval, runoff, and score voting count the same wishes in other ways, and each can pick a different winner.
notes.limits: Arrow showed that no ranked rule is fair in every case, and this ring is no exception.
notes.counter: A rule that finds a compromise can leave nobody glad.
notes.question: What does each rule hide?

sources.label: A Difficulty in the Concept of Social Welfare, Arrow, 1950
A Theory of Measuring, Electing, and Ranking, Balinski and Laraki, 2007
